content.text:
The bug was in `to_cents` in `ledger/currency.py`. It used `int(amount * 100)`, which truncates. `19.99 * 100` evaluates to `1998.9999…`, so it became 1998 instead of 1999. The same truncation made `0.29` come out one cent low per unit, which is why `0.29 × 3` gave 84 instead of 87. It also made the discounted total come out 2 cents low.

I changed it to convert through `Decimal(str(amount))` and round half up to whole cents. All 5 tests now pass, including the two in `tests/test_report.py`. I didn't run any linter or type checker.

`to_cents` rounds half up, so a price with more than two decimal places, such as `0.125`, rounds to the nearest cent instead of truncating.
